 Halloween decorations on Westfield Avenue. JESSICA GRAUE/STAFF
 This year, for the first time since 2020, daylight saving time will end on the same night as Halloween, extending the late night by an hour.
 At 2 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 1, clocks will roll back again to 1 a.m., giving trick-or-treaters an extra hour of sleep and party-goers another hour of celebration.
 Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday in November, which occurs on Nov. 1 every 5-11 years.
 MORE HALLOWEEN COVERAGE: 9 allegedly haunted places to visit in this region and Ohio this Halloween season Lenspricer.com optometrist David Jupiter in a release urged those wearing costume contact lenses to plan ahead for the extra hour and know ahead of time when to take them out.
 “If your recommended wearing time ends at midnight, that’s your curfew. The clock change doesn’t extend it,” Jupiter wrote.
 He also urged party-goers to consider their own fatigue in their plans.
 “Nobody goes out intending to fall asleep in their costume contact lenses,” he said. “It happens when taking them out becomes the last job of the night. You get comfortable, close your eyes for a moment, and wake up hours later.”
 The release added that sleeping while wearing contact lenses increases the risk of eye infections.
 Above all, the release urged partiers wearing lenses to follow the instructions for their lenses and bring a lens case, the recommended solution and glasses (if needed).
